subject.title: Durable Core PR 5/6: add operation-scoped execution recovery

question: Should OpenClaw core own an opt-in shared-state durable execution and recovery subsystem, including operation workers and authority-mode behavior changes, or should this work remain outside core until a maintainer-approved architecture exists?
rationale: The patch creates new durable state, configuration, failure semantics, and cross-owner recovery responsibilities; source-level correctness alone cannot choose the long-term product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Pause for durable-runtime direction
options.body: Do not merge the stack until a responsible maintainer accepts a bounded core ownership, migration, operator, and recovery contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core substrate
options.body: Approve a reduced, explicitly owned core contract and require the branch to remove work outside that accepted boundary before merge.

options.title: Route optional recovery elsewhere
options.body: Keep existing lifecycle owners authoritative and move generalized durable workflow behavior out of OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Pause for durable-runtime direction
recommendation.body: Do not merge the stack until a responsible maintainer accepts a bounded core ownership, migration, operator, and recovery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review context identifies this person as the only evidenced contributor across the directly related durable-stack commits; a repository owner should make the final product decision.
